Within-Subject Mediation Analysis

Source: R/WSMed.R
wsMed.Rd

Performs two-condition within-subject mediation analysis using structural equation modeling (SEM). This function supports multiple types of mediation structures, handles missing data via deletion, FIML, or multiple imputation, and provides both bootstrap and Monte Carlo confidence intervals for unstandardized and standardized effects.

Usage

wsMed(
  data,
  M_C1,
  M_C2,
  Y_C1,
  Y_C2,
  C_C1 = NULL,
  C_C2 = NULL,
  C = NULL,
  form = "P",
  standardized = FALSE,
  Na = "DE",
  ci_method = NULL,
  bootstrap = 1000,
  iseed = 123,
  boot_ci_type = "perc",
  R = 20000L,
  fixed.x = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  alphastd = 0.05,
  m = 5,
  method = "pmm",
  decomposition = "eigen",
  pd = TRUE,
  tol = 1e-06,
  seed = 123,
  MCmethod = NULL,
  store_boot_args = list(),
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame containing the input data.

M_C1

Character vector. Mediator variables under condition 1 (e.g., "before").

M_C2

Character vector. Mediator variables under condition 2 (e.g., "after").

Y_C1

Character. Outcome variable under condition 1.

Y_C2

Character. Outcome variable under condition 2.

C_C1

Character vector of within-subject control variable names (condition 1).

C_C2

Character vector of within-subject control variable names (condition 2).

C

Character vector of between-subject control variable names.

form

Character. Mediation model type: "P", "CN", "CP", or "PC". Defaults to "P".

standardized

Logical. Whether to compute standardized estimates. Defaults to FALSE.

Na

Character. Missing data method: "DE", "FIML", or "MI". Defaults to "DE".

ci_method

Character. Confidence interval method: "bootstrap" or "mc". If NULL, defaults to: "mc" for "MI" amd "FIML", "bootstrap" for "DE".

bootstrap

Integer. Number of bootstrap samples (used for "bootstrap" CI). Defaults to 1000.

iseed

Integer. Random seed used in bootstrapping. Defaults to 123.

boot_ci_type

Character. Type of bootstrap CI: "perc", "bc", or "bca.simple".

R

Integer. Number of Monte Carlo repetitions. Defaults to 20000L.

fixed.x

Logical. Whether to treat predictors as fixed. Defaults to FALSE.

alpha

Numeric vector. Significance levels for CI. Defaults to c(0.01, 0.05).

alphastd

Numeric. Significance level for standardized results. Defaults to 0.05.

m

Integer. Number of imputations for MI. Defaults to 5.

method

Character. Imputation method for mice. Defaults to "pmm".

decomposition

Character. Decomposition method for covariance matrices. Defaults to "eigen".

pd

Logical. Whether to check for positive definiteness. Defaults to TRUE.

tol

Numeric. Tolerance for positive definiteness. Defaults to 1e-06.

seed

Integer. Random seed used in Monte Carlo simulation. Defaults to 123.

MCmethod

Character. If Na = "FIML" and ci_method = "mc", choose "mc" (default) or "bootSD".

Value

A list with class "wsMed" containing:

prepared_data

The preprocessed dataset used for model fitting.

sem_model

Lavaan model syntax used.

lavaan_fit

The fitted lavaan object.

model_summary

Summary statistics from lavaan.

ustd_result

Bootstrap-based unstandardized results (if applicable).

mc_de_result

Monte Carlo results for DE (if applicable).

fiml_result

Monte Carlo results for FIML.

mi_result

Monte Carlo results for MI.

std_result

Standardized bootstrap results (DE or FIML with bootstrap).

std_fiml_result

Standardized MC results for FIML.

std_mi_result

Standardized MC results for MI.

input_vars

Input variable names.

paras

Analysis parameters including alpha, m, method, etc.

ci_method

Chosen CI method.

MCmethod

Chosen MC computation method (for FIML).

Details

The wsMed function is designed for analyzing within-subject mediation models where both mediator and outcome variables are measured under two conditions (e.g., before vs. after intervention).

Key features:

  • Data preprocessing: Automatically computes difference scores and condition-mean scores.

  • Model construction: Supports four types of mediation models:

    • "P": Parallel mediation

    • "CN": Chained mediation

    • "CP": Chained-to-parallel mediation

    • "PC": Parallel-to-chained mediation

  • Missing data strategies:

    • "DE": Listwise deletion of missing values.

    • "FIML": Full Information Maximum Likelihood.

    • "MI": Multiple imputation using the mice package.

  • Inference options:

    • ci_method: Choose "bootstrap" or "mc" (Monte Carlo) for confidence interval estimation. For "MI", only "mc" is supported.

    • MCmethod: For FIML, choose how Monte Carlo is performed:

      • "mc" (default): uses semmcci::MC()

      • "bootSD": uses custom simulation with bootstrap SD correction.

  • Standardized results: Optional standardized estimates with bootstrap or Monte Carlo CI.

Workflow

The function proceeds through the following steps:

  1. Data preprocessing

  2. Model specification

  3. Model fitting

  4. Confidence interval estimation (bootstrap or Monte Carlo)

  5. Optional standardization of results

Examples

data(example_data)
set.seed(123)
example_dataN <- mice::ampute(
 data = example_data,
  prop = 0.1,
  )$amp

result <- wsMed(
  data = example_data,
  M_C1 = c("A2", "B2"),
  M_C2 = c("A1", "B1"),
  Y_C1 = "C1",
  Y_C2 = "C2",
  form = "P",
  Na = "MI",
  standardized = FALSE,
  ci_method = "mc",
  alpha = 0.05,
  alphastd = 0.05
)
#> Error in wsMed(data = example_data, M_C1 = c("A2", "B2"), M_C2 = c("A1",     "B1"), Y_C1 = "C1", Y_C2 = "C2", form = "P", Na = "MI", standardized = FALSE,     ci_method = "mc", alpha = 0.05, alphastd = 0.05): could not find function "wsMed"
print(result)
#> Error: object 'result' not found
